findings.title: AWS S3 sessionToken written to logs in plaintext (1)
findings.detail: Logged in clear text — including archived snapshot(s) edgeFwLog-180826-010028. Anyone with the log bundle can use it while it is valid. Origin: General:publish_backend_api_token. Other secrets in the same messages are masked as ****.
findings.fix: Mask this field in the connector's debug logging; treat existing bundles as sensitive and avoid sharing them outside the team.

playbook.cause: The Cloud Connector writes this secret to its debug log (also in older archived snapshots). It is a logging defect, not a breach by itself — but anyone holding the bundle can use the secret while it is valid.
steps: Treat this bundle as confidential; do not attach it to public tickets.
Tokens expire on their own; rotate if the bundle was shared widely.
Report to Engineering to mask the field in the connector log.

findings.detail: Cards/credentials the controller does not know were presented at 10th IDF, 10th E Elevator Entry.

findings.title: Repeated denials within 60 s — possible credential guessing (5)

playbook.cause: Several denials at one door within a minute — someone guessing PINs, a confused user, or an Aether test sending bad credentials.
steps: If not an Aether test, review camera footage for that door/time.
Consider lockout after N failed PINs.

findings.title: Door forced open (4)
findings.detail: Door opened without a grant, REX or unlock. Doors: 10th IDF, 10th E Elevator Entry.

playbook.cause: The door opened without a grant, REX or unlock. Either someone pushed/pulled the door, the lock did not hold, or a REX device is not wired to the controller.
steps: If this is an Aether test: check the workflow sends a card or REX before driving the DPS.
Verify the lock holds when locked (mechanical/strike power).
Check DPS contact type (NO/NC) in the I/O config matches the wiring.
If people exit with a non-wired REX/crash bar, wire it to the REX input or shunt the alarm.

findings.title: Controller events never published to the cloud (4)
findings.detail: The NHP reported these events to the connector, but no matching RealTime MQTT event followed within 5 s.

playbook.cause: The NHP reported events that never reached the cloud.
steps: Check the cloud event history at those times.
Escalate with the samples.

samples.text: [MQTT messaging.platform.hanwhavision.cloud] Publish Error: Invalid arguments provided.

playbook.cause: "Invalid arguments" publish errors right after first connect to messaging.platform happen during claim/first boot before topics are assigned.
steps: If it only appears once at claim time, ignore.
If it repeats after the device is claimed, escalate with the bundle (connector publishing to an unassigned topic).

findings.title: Unlocks with no grant, REX, schedule or remote command nearby (31)
findings.detail: No access-granted, REX, scheduler transition or incoming cloud message within 3–5 s before the unlock. Could be a manual/remote unlock not logged at DEBUG, or an unexpected relay drive.

playbook.cause: An unlock with no grant, REX or schedule nearby is usually a remote/manual unlock from the cloud or an operator, logged at a level not in this bundle — or an unexpected relay drive.
steps: Check the cloud audit/event history for remote unlocks at these times.
Check schedules that change at these times.
If neither explains it, escalate — unexpected unlocks are a security issue.

symptoms.label: Controller offline
symptoms.desc: Controller shows offline / disconnected in the cloud
checklist: Check power and the network link at the controller (link LEDs, switch port).
Check the site Internet connection at the reported time.
Allow outbound TCP 443 to *.hanwhavision.cloud and UDP 123 (NTP).
If the logs end before the reported time, the controller was likely powered off — check uptime.

symptoms.label: Failure to connect / claim
symptoms.desc: Controller will not connect, register or stay claimed
checklist: Confirm the controller has a correct date/time (NTP) — wrong time breaks TLS and tokens.
Confirm DNS works and *.hanwhavision.cloud resolves from the site.
Check for a TLS-inspecting proxy or firewall on outbound 443.
Re-claim the controller if credentials were rejected.

symptoms.label: Door unlocks unexpectedly
symptoms.desc: Door unlocks or stays unlocked without a valid request
checklist: Check door schedules / unlock overrides active at the reported time.
Check cloud audit history for remote unlocks.
Check REX devices for stuck buttons or PIRs triggering on motion.
Check unlock-on-REX and relock settings on the door.

symptoms.label: Door forced / held alarms
checklist: Check the lock holds when locked (strike power, alignment).
Check DPS contact type (NO/NC) matches the wiring.
Check REX devices are wired so legitimate exits do not alarm.
Check door closer and held-open time.

symptoms.label: Unknown credentials at door
symptoms.desc: Cards/credentials presented that the controller does not recognize
checklist: Confirm the card is enrolled in the cloud and assigned to an access profile for this door.
Check the reader card format (bits / facility code) matches the credential format configured.
Check the credentials have synced to the controller (last sync time).
Repeated unknown cards in a short time → review footage (possible cloning / guessing).

symptoms.label: Valid user denied
symptoms.desc: A known user is refused access
checklist: Check the user's access profile includes this door and the schedule allows the time.
Check the credential is active (not expired / disabled).
Check the controller synced after the profile change.
Check anti-passback rules if enabled.

symptoms.label: Reader offline / not reading
symptoms.desc: Reader beeps, shows offline or does not send card reads
checklist: Check reader power at the reader under load.
Check RS-485 (OSDP) wiring, termination and address/baud, or Wiegand D0/D1.
Confirm the reader port in the cloud matches the physical port.

symptoms.label: Events missing or late in the cloud
symptoms.desc: Door/access events do not appear, or appear late, in the cloud
checklist: Check the door's event filters (ignore access/REX events).
Check whether the controller was offline at that time — events are sent on reconnect.
Compare the controller event time with when it appeared in the cloud.

symptoms.label: Settings / sync not applied
symptoms.desc: Changes made in the cloud do not reach the controller
checklist: Trigger a sync from the cloud and watch for errors in the next scan.
Fix configuration references the logs flag (missing floors, ports, readers).
Check the controller and cloud show the same firmware version.

symptoms.label: Tamper / security concern
symptoms.desc: Tamper alarms, credential guessing or leaked secrets
checklist: Check enclosure tamper switches and cover alignment.
Treat bundles with leaked secrets as confidential; rotate passwords if shared.
Review footage for forced doors / repeated denials.
